title: Rapid notice: data transfer state alignment and evidence routing
text:
Rapid notice: data transfer state alignment and evidence routing

['From: Samir Patel <samir.p@finpulse.com>\\nTo: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>\\nCc: FinPulse Legal <legal@finpulse.com>, Ava Lopez <ava.lopez@forensica.io>\\nDate: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 08:15:00 -0700\\nSubject: RE: notice window — what we need from Redwood\\n\\nBen / Kimberly —\\n\\nThanks for the quick sync this morning. After our internal triage there are two items Legal and our security team want clarified before we can trigger customer notifications:\\n\\n1) Notification scope: is the current draft limited to telemetry/telemetry-derived anomalies, or does it include potential exposure of customer content stored in KV cache?\\n2) Timeline assumptions: your DPA refers to \\"reasonable efforts\\" and a 72-hour notice window for certain incidents — can you confirm the specific clock start (detection vs. confirmed exfiltration)?\\n3) Subprocessor involvement: do any of the subprocessors we rely on (as listed in the April inventory) have independent notification obligations that would alter the timeline or add coordination steps?\\n\\nWe also need a single routing point for evidence exports (SFTP / signed transfer) and a simple matrix mapping evidence types to who at Redwood will accept them (forensics, legal, ops). Ava from Forensica is on the thread to confirm format expectations.\\n\\nIf you can provide those clarifications and an updated evidence-routing matrix, we can confirm our public-facing comms timing.\\n\\nAppreciate urgency — legal is holding on the customer advisory until we have the alignment.\\n\\n—Samir\\n\\nAttachments: none\\n', 'From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>\\nTo: Samir Patel <samir.p@finpulse.com>\\nCc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Grace O\'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Ava Lopez <ava.lopez@forensica.io>, FinPulse Legal <legal@finpulse.com>\\nDate: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 09:05:00 -0700\\nSubject: Re: RE: notice window — what we need from Redwood\\n\\nSamir — thanks, understood. Quick answers up front, then we’ll follow with the matrix and a short call if you want: \\n\\n1) Scope: the active incident we referenced is limited to anomalous service telemetry that flagged an unusual outbound transfer from a worker pool. At present we do not see evidence of KV cache extraction of customer content. We are treating content exposure as a potential escalation path and will update if evidence changes.\\n\\n2) Timeline: for contractual purposes the 72-hour clock in our DPA starts on \\"confirmed compromise\\" — i.e., when our incident response team has validated unauthorized access to customer data. We will communicate interim discovery notices earlier where we have actionable mitigations or containment completed.\\n\\n3) Subprocessors: current publicly shared subprocessor list (attached) shows two third parties used for backups and telemetry aggregation. Both have contractual obligations to notify us within 24 hours of any suspected compromise; however, their notifications will not pause our clock. We will incorporate their notices into a consolidated timeline for customers.\\n\\nNext steps: Kimberley/Kimberly will attach an evidence-routing matrix and a proposed SFTP / signed-hash handoff pattern. Marissa will confirm the legal wording we should use in external notices (specifically how to reference \\"reasonable efforts\\" and the precise start condition). Grace will own the operations handoff if we need a cross-organization export.\\n\\nI’ll set a 30-minute alignment call for 11:30 PT unless you prefer otherwise.\\n\\nThanks —\\nBen Carter\\nAccount Executive, Redwood Inference\\nben.carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0148\\n\\nAttachments: subprocessor-list-2027-04.pdf\\n', "From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>\\nTo: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Samir Patel <samir.p@finpulse.com>\\nCc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Ava Lopez <ava.lopez@forensica.io>, FinPulse Legal <legal@finpulse.com>\\nDate: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 11:20:00 -0700\\nSubject: Re: Re: RE: notice window — what we need from Redwood\\n\\nSamir / team —\\n\\nAttached is the evidence-routing matrix (CSV / XLSX) and an export template we typically use for forensic handoffs. Highlights: \\n\\n- Evidence types and initial owner:\\n  * Service telemetry logs (per instance): SecOps (kimberly.park@redwood.com)\\n  * Inference request metadata (non-content headers): Product Security (grace.oconnor@redwood.com)\\n  * Full payloads / KV snapshots: Legal escalation only — require signed PII transfer form + DPA addendum\\n\\n- Handoff mechanics:\\n  * Preferred: SFTP + SHA256 manifest (incoming from Redwood to FinPulse for joint cases).\\n  * Alternate: AWS S3 presigned URL with short TTL + manifest.\\n  * For high sensitivity (payloads): encrypted disk courier (rare) or direct on-prem export under supervisor sign-off.\\n\\n- Timing: operationally we can prepare a scoped export within 24 hours of a confirmed ask; full payload extractions (if approved) may take 48–72 hours depending on data size and legal signoffs.\\n\\nAva — the CSV includes the column set you requested; please confirm if we need additional hashes or transcript redaction markers.\\n\\nI’ve attached: evidence-routing-matrix.xlsx and export-template.txt\\n\\n—Kimberly\\n\\nAttachments: evidence-routing-matrix.xlsx; export-template.txt\\n", 'From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>\\nTo: Samir Patel <samir.p@finpulse.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>\\nCc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Grace O\'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, FinPulse Legal <legal@finpulse.com>, Ava Lopez <ava.lopez@forensica.io>\\nDate: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 16:02:00 -0700\\nSubject: Re: Re: Re: RE: notice window — what we need from Redwood\\n\\nSamir —\\n\\nLegal quick note to align expectations for customer-facing language and contractual triggers: \\n\\n- \\"Confirmed compromise\\": for DPA wording we will call it \\"confirmed unauthorized access to customer data as determined by Redwood\'s incident response team following forensic validation.\\" That keeps the start tied to our validation while remaining clear to customers.\\n- \\"Reasonable efforts\\": we will avoid ambiguous public phrasing. Proposed line: \\"Redwood will use commercially reasonable and documented incident response procedures to assess, contain, and remediate the incident and will notify Customers as described in the DPA once unauthorized access to Customer Data is confirmed.\\"\\n- Subprocessor cascade: we will state that Redwood coordinates with subprocessors and will include relevant subprocessors in the evidence handoff when their systems are materially implicated. We will not list subprocessors in the public notice unless required by law or the subprocessor\'s incident materially impacts customer data.\\n\\nOperational commitments: we can commit to providing an initial customer notice template within 24 hours of confirmation and an evidence summary to FinPulse within 72 hours of confirmation, subject to receipt of any required subprocessor statements.\\n\\nBen — happy for you to share the attached matrix as discussed. Samir / Legal — let us know if the confirmation wording needs any revision; we can push a brief redline within the hour.\\n\\nMarissa Cole\\nSenior Counsel, Redwood Inference\\nmarissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0192\\n\\nAttachments: updated-notice-draft.txt\\n']
